Morgan (Acme): Hey support — since ~08:10 UTC our requests are way slower and a bunch are 401s. Our app is in us-west but traffic is hitting eu-central and tokens aren't accepted. Any idea?
Emily (Support): Sorry about that, Morgan. Can you paste a request id or last 401? Also roughly when it started?
Morgan (Acme): Request id: req_20260317_081034_az2. Started ~08:10, errors peaked ~08:13. Latency p95 jumped from 80ms->900ms. Header I see: "X-Route-Region: eu-central" but we expected "us-west".
Emily (Support): Thanks. Escalating to SRE. @Raj can you pick up? Adding logs snippet.
Raj (SRE): On it. Can you confirm the API key (prefix) in the req id? I'll look at upstream routing decisions.
Emily (Support): Key prefix: rw-ACME-01.
Raj (SRE): I pulled the trace. The request hit a failover decision that chose eu-central with low latency SLO, then fell back to eu because primary pool returned 503 during a short window. But I'm seeing an oddity: the failover policy we evaluated had the priority array in reversed order compared to the config in console.
Katie (Runtime): Repro note: when the policy payload contains "priority": ["eu-central", "us-west"] but weights are present as strings, our policy deserializer (legacy path) reversed the array if any weight was string-typed. Looks like a migration edge-case.
Raj (SRE): Snippet from the evaluated policy: 
```
{"failover": {"priority": ["eu-central","us-west"], "weights": ["0.3","0.7"], "sticky_ttl": "30s"}}
```
This should have been us-west first. Console shows the intended order but the stored representation was mutated during save.
Victor (Product): Wait — that would explain cross-region hits. Did the canary commit for the new policy editor land last night?
Katie (Runtime): Yes — an API change to accept decimal weights as strings to simplify the UI caused the deserializer to treat string weights as a signal to run the legacy reorder shim. We missed a test that covers mixed/quoted numeric types.
Olga (Billing): FYI we saw a billing spike correlated with the period: egress to eu region is ~4x for this workload. We should rollback asap to avoid more charges.
Raj (SRE): Agreed. Immediate mitigation: 1) Roll back the policy to the last known-good version (I queued rollback commit). 2) Add an explicit regional override for ACME org (pin to us-west) while we patch. 3) Invalidate sticky cookies generated during the 08:10-08:20 window to prevent longer-term affinity to eu.
Emily (Support): Morgan — we rolled back and pinned your org to us-west. Can you confirm latency and 401s now?
Morgan (Acme): Checking now. Initial requests look good. p95 back ~95ms, 401s gone. Thanks.
Raj (SRE): Root cause summary for the ticket: console/API migration allowed numeric weights to be stored as strings; runtime shim detected string-typed weights and triggered a legacy reorder that inverted priority arrays. That inversion caused primary to effectively be second, causing failover to eu on a transient primary glitch. Sticky TTL also parsed as string "30s" and was ignored by some nodes, so affinity didn't recover consistently.
Katie (Runtime): Fix plan: add strict schema validation on write (weights should be numbers or consistently-typed), remove shim that reorders based on type, add unit and integration tests that check ordering across save/load, and a short rollout with canary tests.
Victor (Product): Will also add a console warning if a policy contains mixed-type fields and a migration checklist for the editor.
Olga (Billing): I've opened a billing adjustment ticket for ACME for the 08:10-08:20 egress delta and flagged it high priority.
Emily (Support): Morgan, sorry again for the disruption. We'll keep this thread open until we've validated the permanent fix. Anything else you need?
Morgan (Acme): All good for now. Please let me know when the fix is live so we can close the incident. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: rollout-job/rollback completed for policy:policy_acme_2026-03-17 (status: success)
Raj (SRE): Follow-ups: add a production alert for when priority order in evaluated policy != configured order, and a regression test that simulates stringified weights. Assigning to @Katie.
Katie (Runtime): Got it — I'll start the patch and include the test. ETA for PR: today EOD.
Victor (Product): I'll schedule a postmortem doc and share with Morgan once ready.
Emily (Support): Closing loop with customer once PR merged and patch rolled.
Morgan (Acme): Thanks team, appreciate the quick response.
